title.narrative: School Education Reform Sector Development Program

description.narrative: The program is aligned with the following impact: Human capital that contributes to the country's development and economic growth strengthened. The program will have the following outcome: the ability of the school education system to prepare graduates with subject knowledge and competencies improved. Program and project components both support the following three outputs: Output 1: Quality and relevance of curricula with priority on interdisciplinary approaches improved. The policy-based program component under tranche one supported the government to (i) revise the state standard of general school education, and (ii) set up a regulatory framework for curriculum development. Under tranche two, the program will (iii) approve and roll out new 12-year subject curricula. The project component will help to (i) strengthen the capacity of MES staff and experts on textbook assessment, (ii) build the capacity of the curriculum developers (both institutions and individual experts), (iii) design and implement a step-by-step model for curriculum development review and approval, and (iv) revise the curricula for grades 612. Output 2: Quality of teaching improved. Under tranche one, the policy-based program component supported the government to (i) revise the teacher salary structure and increase teacher salaries; (ii) approve teacher professional standards; and (iii) revise pedagogical university education standards. Under tranche two, the program will (i) incorporate incentives into the teacher salary structure for better performance and continuous professional development, (ii) reform the INSETT system to allow universities to deliver INSETT, and (iii) introduce a fast-track teacher qualification program in universities to bring mid-career professionals into teaching. The project component will (i) help to upgrade pedagogical programs in universities to meet the revised standards and establish international partnerships, (ii) launch INSETT school management and instructional leadership training programs, and (iii) train 10,000 teachers to implement the revised curriculum in schools with a focus on language and STEM.Output 3: Network of Innovative schools strengthened. The policy-based program component supported the government to (i) expand the network of innovative school clusters nationwide (under tranche one); and (ii) provide innovative schools with a special status giving them administrative, academic, and financial autonomy (under tranche two). The project will (i) rehabilitate 23 innovative schools and KAE; (ii) upgrade the STEM and information and communication technology equipment of 23 new and 30 innovative schools, and provide laboratory equipment to 220 cluster schools; (iii) design and implement a training program on school management, instructional leadership, and communication for the school principals and deputy principals of innovative schools; and (iv) train innovative schools and district education managers on effective networking.

Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Network of innovative schools strengthened Indicator: 220 cluster schools provided laboratory equipment to improve teaching STEM Progress/Status: PIU, MES KR, and the 53 innovative schools prepared a list of surrounding cluster schools, which is now under review. A working group was formed in February 2025 to define the STEM laboratory and ICT equipment needed for project schools, and by April 2025, 220 cluster schools and 12 pedagogical universities were officially approved for inclusion. Procurement for laboratory and ICT equipment proceeded through competitive tenders, each receiving one compliant bid, both of which were approved by ADB and contracted in September and August 2025 respectively. During the reporting period, work continued on equipping the 220 cluster schools, including regional coordination meetings and the launch of a commission‑based acceptance process to verify delivered equipment against technical and contractual requirements. Data Source: PIU quarterly project progress reports, and MES orders and Cabinet decrees Actual value:

Output: Network of innovative schools strengthened Indicator: At least 100 raion or town education authorities and all 53 innovative school principals trained on effective network management Progress/Status: The specialist for innovative schools was hired in April 2025. In 2025, several capacity‑building activities were delivered, including strategic planning training for school directors, guidance on completing School Development Strategic Plans, and information sessions on updated subject standards and the “Sanarip Kampa” digital platform. Training was conducted for principals and vice-principals of innovative schools, as well as methodologists from rayon and city education departments, on transformational leadership and innovation management. Data Source: PIU quarterly project progress reports, and MES orders and Cabinet decrees Actual value:

Output: Network of innovative schools strengthened Indicator: Physical infrastructure of 23 schools upgraded to innovative school standards that provide for climate-resilient infrastructure and include female-friendly facilities Progress/Status: The MES KR secured ADB approval to replace two of the originally selected 23 innovative schools, after which the official school list was amended. The PIU Civil Engineer conducted building assessments for all 23 schools and the Kyrgyz Academy of Education, preparing defect reports and initial documentation for renovation. Updated Terms of Reference for design work were approved by ADB, leading to a competitive selection process in which LLC Gradstroyresurs was awarded the contract in September 2025. The firm has since completed the main design and cost‑estimate work, and the full set of design and estimate documentation is expected to be submitted to the PIU by 13 January 2026. Data Source: PIU quarterly project progress reports, and MES orders and Cabinet decrees Actual value:

Output: Network of innovative schools strengthened Indicator: School management of 53 schools including principals and one deputy principal trained in the implementation of the new curriculum with a focus on instructional leadership and gender inclusiveness Progress/Status: In September 2025, the School Management Specialist was hired. The training for leaders of 53 innovative schools was conducted in November 2025. 318 participants were trained. Data Source: PIU quarterly project progress reports, and MES orders and Cabinet decrees Actual value:

Output: Quality and relevance of curricula with priority on interdisciplinary approaches improved Indicator: 34 curricula developers, at least 50% of whom are female, trained and mentored on curricula development that is gender-sensitive and inclusive Progress/Status: In March 2025, the Ministry of Education and Science approved seven working groups—37 specialists in total—to develop STEM subject standards, including 26 experts hired through the PIU. Throughout March and early April, the PIU, KAE, and Okuu Kitebi conducted a series of targeted trainings for adapters and curriculum developers. These sessions covered the State Standard requirements, LTM structure and adaptation processes, gender and inclusion principles, and curriculum design, reaching more than 90 experts across multiple disciplines. Data Source: PIU quarterly project progress reports, number of subject curricula developed, and MES orders and Cabinet decrees Actual value:

Output: Quality and relevance of curricula with priority on interdisciplinary approaches improved Indicator: Capacity of staff (25 from the Kyrgyz Academy of Education, 15 from the Republican Teacher Training Institute, and 7 from the MES Textbook Assessment Center) enhanced Progress/Status: Expected in Q4 2026 Data Source: PIU quarterly project progress reports, number of subject curricula developed, and MES orders and Cabinet decrees Actual value:

Output: Quality of teaching improved. Indicator: 10,000 teachers of STEM subjects trained in implementation of the new curriculum with gender dimensions Progress/Status: In April 2025, the MES and PIU contracted a national expert to support the revision of subject standards and textbooks. To prepare teachers for the new STEM standards and adapted learning materials, a set of professional development resources—including a methodological guide, trainer's manual, and six STEM workbooks—was developed and approved by the RTTI Academic Council in June 2025. The PIU has also requested clarification from the Ministry on whether training 10,000 STEM teachers, as planned in the project, remains feasible given the broader nationwide professional development efforts underway during the transition to a 12‑year education system. Data Source: PIU quarterly project progress reports, number of subject curricula developed, and MES orders and Cabinet decrees Actual value:

Output: Quality of teaching improved. Indicator: 200 university instructors and professors, at least 50% of whom are female, trained as INSETT trainers on implementing new subject curricula in STEM Progress/Status: A national round table was held in December 2024 to discuss reforms in higher pedagogical education as the country transitions to a 12‑year school system, leading to the development of a comprehensive Roadmap for higher, secondary vocational, and postgraduate education reform. To support the rollout of new STEM subject standards and adapted teaching materials, the MES and PIU contracted a national expert in April 2025 and began developing professional development resources, including a methodological guide, trainer's manual, and six STEM workbooks. These materials were approved by the RTTI Academic Council in June 2025. The PIU also initiated steps to integrate the new training modules into the national teacher professional development system, requesting information from RTTI on procedures for hosting the courses on its digital platform. Data Source: PIU quarterly project progress reports, number of subject curricula developed, and MES orders and Cabinet decrees Actual value:

Output: Network of innovative schools strengthened Indicator: Special status for innovative schools that includes (i) additional roles and responsibilities and corresponding financing, as well as (ii) administrative and financial autonomy, identified and approved by MES. Progress/Status: A working group was formed in February 2025 to revise the Model Regulation on Innovative General Education Schools, aiming to strengthen funding mechanisms and grant greater administrative and financial autonomy to support experimental teaching practices. By mid‑2025, the group developed and agreed on key draft documents, including the updated Regulation, performance indicators, and the role of a gender equality coordinator, which were submitted to the Ministry for approval. These drafts were also reviewed by independent experts, and further revisions were made based on their feedback. Throughout the reporting period, the PIU and Working Group continued refining the updated Model Regulation, which was formally submitted to the Ministry in December 2025 for final approval. Data Source: PIU quarterly project progress reports, and MES orders and Cabinet decrees Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Target year: 2027 Target value: Y

They also decided that a detailed roadmap for implementing these improvements will be prepared in 2026. Output: Quality and relevance of curricula with priority on interdisciplinary approaches improved Indicator: Subject curricula for grades 1-12 that include elective options in grades 10-12 based on the revised State Standards of General School Education approved by MES. (2021 baseline: Not based on revised State Standards of General School Education) Progress/Status: The Ministry of Education and Science of the Kyrgyz Republic (MES KR) updated the State Standard of General School Education and issued key orders in early 2025 to guide the development of new STEM subject standards and the adaptation of Marshall Cavendish teaching materials. Terms of Reference, salary regulations, and step‑by‑step guidelines were prepared, and a national call for experts led to the selection of 72 specialists to develop standards and adapt teaching materials. Working groups, coordinated by the Kyrgyz Academy of Education, produced new STEM subject standards, teaching programs, and grade‑7 plans by mid‑2025. These standards were reviewed, approved by the Academic Council, and formally adopted by the Ministry in August 2025 for grades 7-12 in the 12‑year school system. Output: Quality of teaching improved. Indicator: INSETT system restructured to engage more service providers (i.e., at least seven universities). Progress/Status: A working group was formed in February 2025 to reform and streamline the national system for teacher professional development, including restructuring key training institutions and updating related regulations. Throughout 2025, Working Group 2 held several meetings to refine a new professional development model and a draft Roadmap for restructuring the in‑service training system, though its review was postponed for further analysis. Broad consultations were held with representatives from the Ministry, RTTI, universities, and schools, leading to an updated restructuring proposal submitted to the Ministry and then forwarded to the Cabinet of Ministers. The reform envisions consolidating several existing institutions into a new Center for Continuous Professional Development of Teachers to improve service quality and efficiency. Data Source: PIU quarterly project progress reports, number of subject curricula developed, and MES orders and Cabinet decrees Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: TTIs provides INSETT Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: TTIs provides INSETT Target year: 2029 Target value: 7

Output: Quality of teaching improved. Indicator: Incentives for better performance and continuous growth incorporated into teacher salary structure by the Cabinet with its decree. Progress/Status: A working group was created in February 2025 to update regulations on additional higher education and accelerated professional development for teachers, as well as to design mechanisms that support institutional memory and align teacher growth with professional standards. Draft regulatory amendments were prepared and circulated, but their approval was postponed pending a government decision on teacher salary increases expected in April 2026. In parallel, work began on developing digital infrastructure and formalizing teachers' extracurricular tutoring through a new AIS “Mugalim+” module. Data Source: PIU quarterly project progress reports, number of subject curricula developed, and MES orders and Cabinet decrees Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: Y

Output: Quality of teaching improved. Indicator: New PRESETT programs aligned with the new teacher professional standards, and revised state standards for higher professional and school education developed, approved, and launched by seven universities. Progress/Status: A working group was created in February 2025 to reform and streamline the national system for teacher professional development, including reviewing key training institutions and their financing. An expert group was later formed to implement the Roadmap, and by June 2025 the Cabinet of Ministers approved a new Regulation on Additional Higher Education. Following this, a draft Regulation on accelerated professional development was prepared and circulated for feedback, with final approval expected through a joint inter‑agency order. In December 2025, an Interagency Commission was also established to select national consultants to support the transformation of teacher education as the country transitions to a 12‑year schooling system. Data Source: PIU quarterly project progress reports, number of subject curricula developed, and MES orders and Cabinet decrees Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: Y

Output: Quality of teaching improved. Indicator: PRESETT programs revised according to the new (i) school education, (ii) higher education, and (iii) teacher professional standards Progress/Status: The Ministry of Education, together with the PIU, developed a draft roadmap to reform higher and secondary vocational teacher education as the country transitions to a 12‑year school system. By mid‑2025, key analytical reports were completed and shared with the Supervisory Board. To support implementation, the Ministry and PIU requested amendments to the ADB Procurement Plan—approved in September 2025—to fund equipment for innovative schools and hire eight national experts. By late 2025, the selection process for these experts had begun.
